newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to name Army Gen. Clark NATO chief - paper.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to name Army Gen. Clark NATO chief - paper.

text.p: President Bill Clinton has chosen Army Gen. Wesley Clark to become the next top NATO commander and head of U.S. forces in Europe, the Washington Post reported in its Monday edition.
Quoting unidentified senior defence officials, the newspaper said a formal announcement was expected on Monday.

Clark, 52, was the senior military member on the U.S. team, led by diplomat Richard Holbrooke, that brokered the 1995 Dayton peace accords. The agreement stopped the fighting in Bosnia and set terms for the NATO-led peacekeeping force.
Currently Clark, a West Point graduate and former Rhodes scholar at England's Oxford University, heads the Southern Command, which oversees U.S. military operations in Central and South America.
He would replace Gen. George Joulwan, the current NATO commander, who is due to retire this summer.
The Post said Defence Secretary William Cohen recommended Clark for the NATO job after interviewing 13 possible candidates.
